The '''1987–88 Serie A''' was won by [[A.C. Milan|Milan]].

==Teams==
[[Pescara Calcio|Pescara]], [[Pisa Calcio|Pisa]] and [[AC Cesena|Cesena]] had been promoted from [[Serie B]].

== Season summary ==
The summer of 1987 brought several notable players into the Italian championship: [[Vincenzo Scifo]] (for [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]]), [[Ian Rush]] ([[Juventus FC|Juventus]]), [[Ruud Gullit]] and [[Marco van Basten]] ([[A.C. Milan|Milan]]).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/09/12/giorni-del-calcio.html|title=I giorni del calcio|author=Gianni Brera|work=[[la Repubblica]]|date=12 September 1987|pages=1|language=italian}}</ref> The reigning champions [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] started well leading the league after five matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/10/13/il-fenomeno-napoli.html|title=Il fenomeno Napoli|author=Gianni Mura|work=la Repubblica|date=13 October 1987|pages=23|language=italian}}</ref> Inter and Juventus had several issues.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/10/27/qualcosa-di-travolgente.html|title=Qualcosa di travolgente|author=Gianni Brera|work=la Repubblica|date=27 October 1987|pages=45|language=italian}}</ref>

Napoli retained top-place in autumn and winter, suffering only one defeat in the first 20 games.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/11/03/maradona-padre-nostro.html|title=Maradona padre nostro|author=Gianni Brera|work=la Repubblica|date=3 November 1987|pages=35|language=italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/11/24/caro-napoli-vai-troppo-forte.html|title=Caro Napoli, vai troppo forte|author=Gianni Brera|work=la Repubblica|date=24 November 1987|pages=33|language=italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1987/12/24/da-boniperti-complimenti-al-napoli.html|title=Da Boniperti complimenti al Napoli|work=la Repubblica|date=24 December 1987|pages=19|language=italian}}</ref> Napoli began to struggle in March, and ultimately only won 2 of the 10 remaining fixtures. Milan who had been in second place for much of the season were able to reduce the points deficit with a prolonged undefeated run.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1988/03/22/favole-per-la-primavera.html|title=Favole per la primavera|author=Gianni Brera|work=la Repubblica|date=22 March 1988|pages=23|language=italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1988/04/19/vi-da-fastidio-lo-scudetto-bis.html|title=Vi dà fastidio lo scudetto bis?|author=Gianni Mura|work=la Repubblica|date=19 April 1988|pages=34|language=italian}}</ref> Their head-to-head match, played on 1 May 1988, ended in a 3–2 win for Milan putting them 1 point ahead in the title race with two games remaining to play.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1988/05/03/ma-non-ancora-scudetto.html|title=Ma non è ancora scudetto|author=Licia Granello|work=la Repubblica|date=3 May 1988|pages=34|language=italian}}</ref> Milan drew their final games, but Napoli did worse, losing both matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1988/05/15/la-rivoluzione-del-sor-capanna.html|title=La rivoluzione del sor Capanna|author=Gianni Mura|work=la Repubblica|date=15 May 1988|pages=23|language=italian}}</ref> It led to Milan's 11th title and its first since 1979.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1988/05/17/juve-ancora-lacrime.html|title=Juve, ancora lacrime|author=Massimo Agostini|work=la Repubblica|date=17 May 1988|pages=26|language=italian}}</ref> This season was the last with 16 teams playing, as two relegations and four promotions from [[Serie B]] meant that from 1988–89 there would be 18 clubs in the top flight.
